head: Anyone could buy in.
Few got a say.
slides.sub: How a Dutch trading company made shares something you could sell.

image.label: A thick ledger open on a desk in a 1600s Dutch office
image.brief: 17세기 초 네덜란드 사무실 책상 위에 펼쳐진 두꺼운 청약 장부와 깃펜. 창밖으로 운하와 범선 돛대가 보임. 렘브란트풍의 어둡고 따뜻한 빛. 실존 인물 얼굴 없음.

head: One ship, one fund,
then split the spices.
body: In the 1590s, Dutch merchants began sending ships to Asia for pepper and nutmeg. Each small company raised money for a voyage and shared out the profits when the ships came home, if they came home.
Rival Dutch firms bid against each other in Asia and pushed prices up.

image.label: Dutch sailing ships leaving a harbor in grey weather
image.brief: 1590년대 네덜란드 항구를 떠나는 범선들. 회색 하늘과 거친 바다, 부두에서 배웅하는 사람들의 실루엣.

head: The government said:
merge.
body: In 1602, pushed by the States General, the rival firms merged into the United East India Company, the VOC. Its charter gave it a monopoly on Dutch trade with Asia for 21 years.
Long-distance trade on that scale needed fleets, forts and patient money.

image.label: Merchants in dark coats around a table signing papers
image.brief: 검은 외투와 주름 깃 차림의 상인들이 탁자에 둘러앉아 문서에 서명하는 장면. 얼굴은 그림자나 뒷모습으로 처리.

head: You need money for years,
not one voyage.
body: A round trip to Asia can take years. Forts and fleets pay back slowly. How do you fund it?

options.text: Keep funding voyage by voyage from a few rich merchants
options.feedback: Familiar and easy to control, but each fund ends when the ships return, and the money leaves with it. Keep swiping.

options.text: Borrow heavily from lenders and the state
options.feedback: No new owners to answer to, but interest is due whether ships sink or not. Keep swiping.

options.text: Sell shares to anyone, and lock the money in for ten years
options.feedback: Locked money is patient, but investors may not want to wait that long. Keep swiping.

image.label: A merchant weighing coins beside a map of Asia
image.brief: 아시아 지도 옆에서 동전을 저울에 다는 상인의 손. 촛불 조명, 17세기 분위기.

slides.label: people signed the Amsterdam subscription book in August 1602
body: Any resident of the Dutch Republic could buy in. The Amsterdam list has wealthy merchants, but also craftsmen, shopkeepers and, reportedly, a housemaid.

image.label: A line of ordinary townspeople waiting outside a house
image.brief: 암스테르담 운하 주택 앞에 줄 선 다양한 계층의 시민들. 상인, 장인, 앞치마 두른 여성의 뒷모습.

slides.label: guilders raised in total, about, far more than earlier voyage firms
body: The money could not be taken out before a first accounting, planned after ten years. That gave the company patient capital. It also gave investors a problem: what if they needed cash?

image.label: Stacked chests of coins in a counting room
image.brief: 계산실에 쌓인 동전 상자들과 자물쇠. 차갑고 단단한 느낌의 빛.

head: Can’t cash out?
Sell to someone else.
body: Investors found an exit: sell their shares to other people. The company recorded each transfer in its books. Buyers and sellers met in the streets and on a bridge in Amsterdam, and by 1611 the city had a purpose-built exchange.
Prices rose and fell with news from Asia.

image.label: A crowded stone courtyard of traders in the 1600s
image.brief: 1600년대 아케이드로 둘러싸인 돌 마당에 모인 거래인들. 손짓으로 흥정하는 군중의 실루엣.

head: Owners without
a real voice.
body: Directors ran the company and shared few accounts. The first dividend came only in 1610, and part of it was paid in spices.
When shareholders protested at the charter renewal in the early 1620s, they won only limited changes.

image.label: A closed door with light under it and people waiting outside
image.brief: 불빛이 새어 나오는 닫힌 이사회실 문, 그 앞 복도에서 기다리는 사람들의 실루엣.

head: A trading giant,
then bankrupt.
body: The VOC grew into a vast power in Asia, and it used force to get there, including the brutal conquest of the Banda Islands in 1621.
Debts piled up during the 1700s. The Dutch state took it over, and the company was dissolved at the end of 1799.

image.label: A decaying warehouse by a canal at dusk
image.brief: 해 질 녘 운하 옆 낡아 가는 창고. 빈 향신료 자루와 녹슨 닻. 쓸쓸한 톤.

head: Easy exit fixed waiting.
It didn’t fix oversight.
body: Locking capital in let the VOC plan in decades. Tradable shares let investors leave without pulling money from the company. Stock markets still rest on that pairing.
But the right to sell is not the right to see or steer. With little oversight, problems could grow out of view.

image.label: A door marked exit beside a window that is shuttered
image.brief: 열린 출구 문과 덧문이 닫힌 창문이 나란히 있는 상징적 그래픽. 17세기 네덜란드 건축 질감.

head: Give backers a way out,
and a way to look in.
body: Patient money needs both an exit and honest information, or trust wears thin.
**Try it today:** list who has put money or time into your business. What can they actually see, and how could they step away if they had to?

image.label: A single ship on calm water at sunrise
image.brief: 해 뜨는 잔잔한 바다 위 범선 한 척. 차분하고 희망적인 톤.

factChecks.note: '최초의 IPO'는 흔히 쓰는 표현이지만 논쟁이 있습니다. 영국 동인도회사(1600)나 그 이전의 합자회사도 있었습니다. VOC는 공화국 주민 누구나 청약할 수 있었고, 장기 고정자본과 양도 가능한 지분을 결합한 사례로 자주 꼽힙니다. 그래서 카드에서는 'IPO'라는 말을 직접 쓰지 않았습니다.
1602년 3월 선행 회사들의 합병, 전국의회(States General)의 압력, 21년 독점 특허장은 Gaastra(2003) 등 표준 연구서로 확인하세요. → [2026-11-02 확인] 1602년 3월 20일 21년 특허장 확인.
암스테르담 청약자 '1,100명 이상'(Petram 2014에 따르면 1,143명)과 청약 시기(1602년 8월)를 확인하세요. '가정부가 청약했다'는 Petram이 소개한 청약 장부 사례로, 카드에는 reportedly로 표시했습니다. → [2026-11-02 확인] Petram: 암스테르담 청약자 1,143명 확인. 청약 마감 1602년 9월 1일.
총 자본금 약 640만 길더(흔히 6,424,588길더로 인용)는 전체 지부(chamber) 합계입니다. 카드에는 'about 6.4 million'으로 적었습니다. → [2026-11-02 확인] 총 자본금 약 640만 길더 확인.
10년 뒤 첫 정산 계획, 회사 장부를 통한 지분 이전, 1611년 암스테르담 거래소 건물 개장은 Petram(2014)과 Gelderblom·de Jong·Jonker(2013)로 확인하세요.
첫 배당(1610년, 일부를 향신료로 지급)과 1620년대 초 특허장 갱신 때 주주 항의의 결과가 제한적이었다는 점은 Gelderblom 외(2013) 기준입니다. → [2026-11-02 확인] 1610년 첫 배당 일부 향신료 지급은 이번 검색에서 미확인.
1621년 반다 제도 정복의 폭력성, 18세기의 부채 누적, 국가 인수(1796)와 1799년 말 해산은 표준 연구서로 확인하세요. 카드에는 국유화 연도를 적지 않았습니다.

sources.text: Petram, L. (2014). The World’s First Stock Exchange. Columbia University Press.
Gelderblom, O., de Jong, A. & Jonker, J. (2013). The Formative Years of the Modern Corporation: The Dutch East India Company VOC, 1602–1623. Journal of Economic History.
Gaastra, F. S. (2003). The Dutch East India Company: Expansion and Decline. Walburg Pers.
